No ambient ring or field, no homogeneity or degree condition, no nilpotency hypothesis, and no phrase such as for all sufficiently large m are part of this problem; those notions are inapplicable here and should not be added. ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
refined_question: For fixed integers r >= 1 and n >= 0, let P range over all r-differential posets in Stanley's standard sense, i.e. locally finite posets with a unique minimum 0-hat such that: (i) if an element covers k elements, then it is covered by k + r elements; and (ii) if two distinct elements both cover exactly t elements, then exactly t elements cover both of them. What is the minimum possible cardinality |P_n| of the nth rank P_n? Is this minimum attained by Y^{×r}, where Y denotes Young's lattice of integer partitions and Y^{×r} its r-fold Cartesian product? ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
